Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

### ① Derived judgments

**No second judge (ruling B) — holds.** Nothing under `ui/` in the diff evaluates `when`; the only `when` touch under `ui/` on main remains the Studio editor preserving the key. `RecordFieldAccessScope.scoped` (RecordFieldAccessScope.tsx:398-447) replaces exactly one input of `checkField`: for `action === 'write'`, the scoped object (case-folded, as `MePermissionsProvider` folds), a field that is not `SystemFieldName.OWNER_ID` (`'owner_id'`, system-names.ts:173) and that `/auth/me/permissions` reports with an explicit `write === false` entry (`lockedByEntry` over `parent.getFieldPermissions`, which is the raw `fields` map with `editable !== false`, MePermissionsProvider.tsx:407-424), the answer is `editable.has(field)` from the server's record projection. Every other case returns `parent.checkField`: a field with no entry keeps the object-grant fallback (`allowEdit`, MePermissionsProvider.tsx:360-371), the owner field keeps the transfer-grant rule (objectui#12103, lines 324-339), `read` and `create` keep the enclosing answer, other objects are untouched, and `check`, `can`, `getFieldPermissions`, `getObjectApiOperations`, `effectiveObjects`, `isLoaded` are spread through. Edit-dialog consumers all reach it through `usePermissions()`: `fieldWriteGate` and `gateFormFields` → `applyFieldPermissions` → `gateByPermission` → `resolveFieldAffordance('editFormFields', …)` → `checkField(object, field, 'write')` (fieldWriteGate.ts, affordanceGrants.ts:132,320-328); `managedModeLocked` reads `can(object, 'update')` plus the managed bucket and `apiOperations`, none of which the scope touches, so the form-wide lock is unchanged. The three wrappers (ModalForm.tsx:316-321, ObjectForm.tsx:248-253, DrawerForm.tsx:236-241) mount `RecordFieldAccessForForm` above the unchanged bodies, which is above every `usePermissions()` in `ObjectFormBody`, `SimpleObjectForm`, `TabbedForm`, `SplitForm`, `WizardForm`, `MasterDetailForm`, `ModalFormBody`, `DrawerFormBody`. `RecordFieldAccessForForm` (recordFieldAccess.tsx:40-54) asks only when `schema.mode === 'edit'`, `objectName` and a non-empty `recordId` are present and the data source has the method; a create form, a `view` form, a form with no record id and a non-ObjectStack data source render their children unwrapped. The master-detail header `ObjectForm` (MasterDetailForm.tsx:2088, `parentSchema` carries `mode` and `recordId`) and `ObjectFormBody`'s own `modal` / `drawer` dispatch carry the same (object, record) key and are detected as nested (`SCOPE_OF`), so one ask per record; the master-detail row editor (MasterDetailForm.tsx:2145, `mode: 'edit'`, no `recordId`) asks nothing. Cases walked for a field and row where the dialog and the server's field-level answer disagree: `summary` conditioned, draft row → entry locked, `editable` has it → enabled, saved (pinned, both containers); `summary`, approved row → `editable` lacks it → locked; `ref_no` unconditioned → entry locked, `editable` lacks it on both rows → locked; `title` no entry → object grant, `editable` has it → enabled; a field in `editable` whose entry says `editable: true` (a set the server's fold still refuses) → the row-blind answer stands, as before; a field the answer omits that no entry locks → object grant, as before (pinned in RecordFieldAccessScope-26594 case 4); `owner_id` in `editable` → transfer rule (pinned). None found where the dialog enables a field the server's field-level answer locks while an answer is held, nor the reverse. The designer forms (ObjectManager.tsx:228, FieldDesigner.tsx:410) have `mode: 'edit'` and no `recordId`, so they ask nothing.

**The outbound save gate — holds.** `ModalFormBody.handleSubmit` (ModalForm.tsx:703-724 on main) and `SimpleObjectForm.handleSubmit` build `canEdit = fieldWriteGate(perms, objectName, mode)` from the same `perms` the render pass reads, then `sanitizeFormData(data, objectSchema, { canEdit })` and `dirtyEditPayload`. A field the answer locks is stripped (`ref_no`, pinned absent from `update`'s payload), a field it unlocks passes (`summary`, pinned present with the edited value). `dirtyEditPayload` sends only changed fields, so an unlocked field left unchanged is omitted by design, not dropped. MasterDetailForm's batch reads `usePermissions()` below the scope (MasterDetailForm.tsx:871). No path found where an unlocked, edited field is silently dropped.

**Fallbacks — fail-closed, with one stale-answer window (③ flag 1).** Pending: `answer` is `null` until `load` settles → `scoped(parent, …, null)` → `{ ...parent }`, the row-blind lock (pinned). No answer: `null`/`undefined`/non-array `editable` and a rejection all set `null` (RecordFieldAccessScope.tsx:486-487). The adapter maps the record read's 404 (`is404Error`: `httpStatus`/`status`/`statusCode` 404 or `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`/`RECORD_NOT_FOUND`) and a 501 / `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` to `null`, rethrows anything else (a 403, pinned), which the scope then also treats as no answer — a refused projection keeps the lock silently (③ flag 4). Record id change while open: the effect is keyed on `key = JSON.stringify([object.toLowerCase(), recordId])`, `current` reads `answer.key === key ? value : null`, so the new record is locked until its own answer lands, and the `alive` flag discards a superseded resolution. Two dialogs: each instance holds its own state; the module cache is keyed on (parent value, key, answer object), so they share nothing but a derived value. The answer is keyed by object and record id. The in-place record re-read is the gap: both `ModalFormBody` and `SimpleObjectForm` re-read the record through `useRecordInvalidation` (`recordRefetch`, and `recordSaved()` after their own save) while the scope's effect depends on `[!!parent, nested, key]` alone, so a re-read that moves the row into the state `when` names leaves the earlier `editable` standing. See ③ flag 1 for the window and the fix.

**The row-not-writable case — honest, not worse.** The dev's measurement is real (dogfood new leg: `GET /data/rfa_notice/:id` 200, `field-access` lists `title` and `summary`, `PATCH` 403) and the ui reading is confirmed in the code: no ui surface gates the edit dialog on row-level write scope; `managedModeLocked` reads `can(object, 'update')`, the object grant only. On such a row the only field input the scope replaces is the explicit field-level lock, which on `rfa_notice` has no entries, so the dialog's answer is byte-identical to before this PR. Documented where asked: `RecordFieldAccess.editable` (data.ts:1066-1072: "The object grant, the record's row-level write scope and a field's own rules … are not part of it"), the scope's doc (RecordFieldAccessScope.tsx:464-469, a ⛔ paragraph), the plugin-form changeset's last sentence, and the FLS doc bullet (field-level-security.mdx:75-79). No sentence in the diff claims the dialog never offers an edit the server refuses; the scope doc's "disabled exactly where the write gate refuses it" is scoped by the paragraph below it to field-level, and the test headers say "disables only what that answer locks".

**Contract use — holds.** `ObjectStackAdapter.getRecordFieldAccess(resource, id)` calls `client.data.fieldAccess(resource, String(id))`, which on main builds `${baseUrl}${getRoute('data')}/${encodeURIComponent(object)}/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/field-access` and unwraps the `{ success, data }` envelope (client index.ts:7415-7421); the pinned URL `…/data/rfa_contract/c%2F1/field-access` matches the merged route `GET {dataPath}/:object/:id/field-access` (data-action-routes.ts:354-400), whose answer is `{ object, recordId, readable, editable }` and which the `RecordFieldAccess` type mirrors field for field. The client's private `fetch` adds `Authorization`, `X-Environment-Id` and `Accept-Language` on every request (index.ts:7520-7544), so tenancy rides the same path as every other data read. Error mapping read above.

**The handler-key census fix — honest.** `documentCarryingChildren` (check-handler-key-read-sites.mjs:1023-1038) follows a child only when its `schema=` attribute carries the parent's own document (`documentIdentifiers` seeds `schema`); a `{...props}` spread is a declared non-answer of that gate (header boundary 1). The wrappers' first spelling spread the document, so the hop to the body was lost and the `view:form` / `object-form` reads fell out of the census; passing `schema={schema}` by name beside `{...rest}` restores the hop to the same body with the same reads. Nothing was declared, exempted or baselined; the three wrappers read no handler key themselves. `Type Check UI` runs the source-parsing gates on the PR and is the CI reading of the 56 (③ gate reading).

**Declarations — hold.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body and on the three widening changesets; `Clause-②: no` on `@object-ui/plugin-form`, which adds no public surface. `Ruling-ref: 6457467702`. `Skills-docs: updated here — …`: the value's first word is a recognised form; its claim is true on main — `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md:182-208` teaches `when` and names no reader of the lock (no `/auth/me/permissions`, no projection), and no `skills/**` path is touched, so the PR is not governed. Changesets live in the root `.changeset/`, which is the configured root (`.changeset/config.json` lists the `@object-ui/*` packages in its `fixed` groups; `ui/.changeset/` holds legacy files and a README with no `config.json`), and `Check Changeset` is green. `Fixes #26594`: the card's Expected ("the record form's field projection judges `when` against the record being edited") is delivered for the edit dialog (`ModalForm`, the console's dialog), the edit page (`ObjectForm` and every layout) and `DrawerForm`. Left of the card: the record detail page's inline edit (`plugin-detail` `recordEdit`) holds one row and still reads the row-blind lock — the dev names it as an out-of-scope finding but files no issue (③ flag 2).

**Tests.** `recordFieldAccess-26594.test.tsx` (10 = 5 × 2 containers) renders `ModalForm` directly as `AppContent` mounts it and `ObjectForm`'s edit page under `MePermissionsProvider` with the row-blind persona and a stubbed data source, and pins what the ruling asks: draft unlock + unconditioned lock + one ask with `('rfa_contract', 'c1')`; the save's payload; the approved row locked after the ask; create asks nothing; no method keeps the lock. `RecordFieldAccessScope-26594.test.tsx` (7) is the truth table including pending / `null` / rejected → locked, nested asks once, no provider asks nothing. `getRecordFieldAccess-26594.test.ts` (4): URL encoding, envelope, 404 → null, 501 → null, 403 thrown. `affordanceGrantMap-12082.test.tsx`: the write census keys sites by `FILE :: enclosing symbols :: VERB` and fails on an unlisted or gone site (lines 1060-1069); the four `ModalForm`/`DrawerForm` `handleSubmit` rows move to `ModalFormBody`/`DrawerFormBody` with the same disposition (`mapped([...], FIELD_WRITE_GATE)`) — nothing weakened, and the rename is what the census demands. The dogfood leg is honest and does not run on the PR path (③ flag 3). The reported ablation (pass-through wrapper → 6 red / 4 green) is the predicted shape: draft unlock, save, approved-row-after-ask in both containers depend on the scope; create and no-method do not.

**Gates.** The dev's 93 derived / 93 run / 0 NOT-MEASURED reading was taken on this head (`90f1ea4df`, one commit on `a98daf75f`), with the one first-run red (`pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run scripts/`, the census above) rerun green after the by-name fix that is in the head. The head has not moved, so the reading carries; the check-runs are the verdicts of record and are read in ③.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@object-ui/types`, `@object-ui/data-objectstack`, `@object-ui/permissions`, `@object-ui/plugin-form` — correct under the repo's rule: the level follows the declared kind alone, and `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3). Read as plain semver the first three add public surface (an optional `DataSource` member and a type, an adapter method, an exported component) and would be `minor`; the four packages sit in the root `fixed` groups, so the published number is the group's either way. No BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 marker owed: nothing is removed, narrowed or re-meant.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Stale projection after an in-place record re-read (ask: fix in a follow-up card before or at landing; not a FAIL).** `RecordFieldAccessScope` asks once per (object, record) and never again, while the form it wraps re-reads the record in place — `useRecordInvalidation` moves `recordRefetch` on a bus change while pristine and replays a held one on `recordSaved()` after the form's own save (recordInvalidation.ts; ModalForm.tsx:517-600; ObjectForm.tsx:889-973). A form that stays mounted after a save that moves the row into the state `when` names (an SDUI `view:form` or `ScreenView`'s form with no `onSuccess`, which stay mounted and filled), or a pristine dialog whose record the bus re-reads after a same-tab write, then draws the conditioned field enabled from the earlier `editable` and the server refuses the save — the opposite polarity of the card's symptom, in a window that did not exist under the row-blind lock. The console's own paths close or navigate on success (`AppContent` keys the dialog by record id and closes it; `RecordFormPage` passes `handleSuccess`), so the window is narrow there. The fix is small and local: re-ask when the record is re-read (hand the scope the form's `recordRefetch` nonce or the loaded record snapshot as part of its key, or clear the answer on `recordSaved`), and pin it with one more leg of `recordFieldAccess-26594.test.tsx`. The PR body's fail-closed claim ("until the answer arrives, and when there is none, the row-blind lock stands") is true as written; it does not claim the answer follows the record, and the docs do not say it does.
2. **Residual of the card, not filed (ask).** The record detail page's inline edit (`plugin-detail` `DetailSection.tsx:507`, `HeaderHighlight.tsx:211`, `resolveFieldAffordance('recordEdit', …)`) holds one row and shows the card's symptom (a conditioned lock drawn on a draft). The dev lists it under `out_of_scope_findings` with no issue number. AGENTS.md #10: a reproducible defect is filed, not noted. The owning seat should file it as the card's residual (and the list inline edit's per-column lock as a declared limitation, since one column lock cannot split per row). `Fixes #26594` stands for the edit dialog, which is what the card measured.
3. **Dogfood not on the PR path (acknowledged).** `record-field-access-when.dogfood.test.ts` runs on `main`'s full battery only; its 8/8 is the dev's local reading. The new leg's assertions were read against the fixture (`rfa_notice` `public_read`, inserted by `SYS`, member holds the object grant) and are consistent with the route's declared scope. The first full-battery run after merge is its gate reading.
4. **A refused projection is silent.** A 403 (or any non-404/501 refusal) from `getRecordFieldAccess` is rethrown by the adapter and swallowed by the scope into "no answer"; the lock stands, which is the safe side, but nothing logs it. Acceptable for a UX-only input whose server boundary is unchanged; noted so a later reader does not mistake the lock for the server's verdict.
5. **Dev deviations accepted.** Branch `claude/project-thread-dyw8uu` in place of `claude/issue-26594-<slug>` (measured platform constraint, declared in the claim). Human Minimum item 3 left unchecked with `pnpm lint` named as CI's run: `Lint UI` and `Lint · ESLint` are the readings (③ 7). The first-run red of the ui `scripts/` gate was fixed in the head and rerun green; the fix is the by-name `schema=` read above.
6. **Semver reading** as in ②: `patch` by the repo's rule, `minor` by plain semver on three of the four; the rule binds.

### ① Derived judgments

**The window is closed, fail-closed on both paths.** `RecordFieldAccessScope` gains `revision` (default 0). The ask effect now depends on `[!!parent, nested, key, revision]`, each resolution is tagged with the revision it was asked under, and `current` reads `answer.key === key && answer.revision === revision ? value : null` (RecordFieldAccessScope.tsx:168-190). So on the very render in which `revision` moves, `current` is `null`, `scoped(parent, …, null)` is `{ ...parent }`, and every conditioned field is drawn from the row-blind lock until the new answer lands: there is no render between the revision moving and the new answer in which the earlier `editable` is read. A superseded resolution cannot land: the effect's cleanup sets `alive = false` for the earlier run, and a resolution that did slip through would carry an older `revision` and be ignored by the equality. `RecordFieldAccessForForm` moves the revision on two signals (recordFieldAccess.tsx:56-71): (a) `useDataInvalidation(objectName, id)` — the same bus nonce `useRecordInvalidation` reads for the form's re-read (data-invalidation.ts: a change for this record, for the object, or `'*'`; a sibling record does not match), so every bus re-read of the record is a re-ask too, and (b) the data source's `onMutation`, filtered to events whose `resource` is this object (case-folded) and whose `id`, when present, is this record; an id-less event (the adapter's bulk `update`/`delete` emit `{ type, resource }` only) also moves it, which is the conservative direction. The adapter emits `update` after the client write resolves and before `update()` returns (data-objectstack index.ts:4405-4414), so on the form's own save the revision moves before `advanceLoadedRecord` and `recordSaved()` run, independent of whether a host mounts the console's bridge (`useMutationInvalidationBridge`, AppContent.tsx:705). A different record's write: filtered by `id` on `onMutation`; filtered by `dataChangeMatches` on the bus. Covered by both signals: the own-save path (onMutation, and the bridge on the console), the bus re-read path (any same-tab writer that notifies this record or object). Not covered, as before: a change made by another client — no signal reaches this tab, the form does not re-read either, and the server refuses the save; this is the pre-existing shape of every client-side reader and is not new to this PR.

**No storm, no loop.** The re-ask is a GET through `getRecordFieldAccess`; the adapter emits no mutation for it and nothing notifies the bus, so a re-ask cannot trigger itself.
